title: Restore unassisted erectile function after a finite treatment

concept.text: Durably restore erections in chronic vasculogenic or post-prostatectomy ED after treatment has ended. Regenerative approaches have clinical signals, but reliable, durable recovery without erection aids remains unestablished. Proposed completion test: Regulatory approval for restoration of untreated function following a sham-controlled pivotal trial of at least 300 men: at least 50% achieve normal-range IIEF-EF scores and successful unassisted intercourse at 12 months, after at least three months without erection aids. Post-prostatectomy efficacy requires a separately powered analysis. Test set by: Proposed editorial completion test using validated sexual-function outcomes; FDA would decide an approval claim. EAU and SMSNA identify the need for better controlled evidence on restorative therapies. Sources given: [EAU erectile dysfunction guideline](https://uroweb.org/guidelines/sexual-and-reproductive-health/chapter/management-of-erectile-dysfunction) ; [SMSNA restorative-therapy position statement](https://academic.oup.com/smoa/article/9/3/100343/6956862).

page.title: Restoration of unassisted erectile function
page.definition: A finite treatment restores erections sufficient for intercourse in men with chronic vasculogenic erectile dysfunction, caused by impaired penile blood flow, or erectile dysfunction after radical prostatectomy, removal of the prostate. Erections continue after treatment ends without drugs, injections, vacuum devices or penile implants.

goal.need: The EAU identifies 18 phase I–II studies of stem-cell treatment involving 373 participants. Only four were placebo-controlled, and their efficacy findings conflicted. Establishing recovery after treatment ends therefore requires evidence beyond the safety observations and uncontrolled improvements reported in these studies.

figures.note: These ranges summarize different studies and are not complementary outcomes from one cohort.

statements.quote: There is no evidence that penile rehabilitation itself increases the chances of spontaneous EF recovery in men following nerve-sparing RP
statements.context: EF means erectile function; RP means radical prostatectomy. The passage concerns postoperative rehabilitation.

statements.body: Sexual Medicine Society of North America
statements.quote: Sexual medicine providers recognize the importance of restoring spontaneous physiologic erections.

completion.title: A regulator authorises a finite treatment for sustained unassisted erectile recovery.
completion.criterion: A regulator authorises a finite treatment with an indication explicitly covering sustained erections sufficient for intercourse after treatment ends, without erection drugs, injections, vacuum devices or penile implants. The authorised population and demonstrated treatment-free duration must be specified in the indication or supporting assessment. Achievement is recorded separately for vasculogenic and post-prostatectomy erectile dysfunction; an authorisation for one does not establish the other.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback, following SMSNA's support for regulatory evaluation of restorative treatments; no common restoration-specific completion threshold was found.
completion.basis: Searches of EAU and SMSNA recommendations, FDA development requirements and trial registrations found no common cure test specifying a responder fraction, washout interval and duration after finite treatment. SMSNA supports regulatory approval based on safety and efficacy studies. The fallback requires authorisation for the restorative capability itself, with product-specific evidence defining its duration.

milestones.title: A candidate improves nerve-stimulated penile pressure relative to blood pressure at P < 0.05.
milestones.criterion: Treatment increases intracavernous pressure divided by mean arterial pressure (ICP/MAP) versus ED vehicle controls. Albersen's protocol assessed this at four weeks using P < 0.05: cells and cell lysate improved responses in 32 rats allocated to four equal groups. A separate vasculogenic study enrolled 38 rats, including 28 with diet-induced hyperlipidaemia, and found improved ICP/MAP 28 days after cell injection. The nerve-injury experiment treated animals immediately after injury and did not model established chronic ED.
milestones.set_by: University of California, San Francisco, published controlled animal-study protocol of Albersen et al.; its four-week timing concerns cavernous-nerve injury. ESSM endorses ICP/MAP measurement, without defining a universal recovery cutoff.
milestones.threshold_quote: Results were considered statistically significant if p<0.05.

milestones.title: Men receive a finite restorative treatment in a phase I study with prospective safety follow-up.
milestones.criterion: A candidate is administered to men under an approved phase I protocol with safety and tolerability as its primary endpoint. NCT02240823 followed 17 men for six months after one intracavernous injection of autologous adipose-derived regenerative cells, 5–18 months after prostatectomy. No serious adverse events were observed. Participants could continue or retry erection medication, so the reported sexual-function improvements do not establish unassisted restoration.
milestones.set_by: Odense University Hospital, registered phase I protocol NCT02240823, published for post-prostatectomy ED.
milestones.threshold_quote: Primary endpoint was the safety and tolerance of the cell therapy

milestones.title: A finite treatment increases six-month erectile-function responders over placebo without erection aids.
milestones.criterion: Compare responder proportions six months after the final treatment while other ED treatments are prohibited, using two-sided P < 0.05. A responder gains ≥2 IIEF-EF points from baseline scores of 17–25, or ≥5 points from scores of 11–16. IIEF-EF is the six-item erectile-function domain of the International Index of Erectile Function. In the 2021 platelet-rich plasma study, 60 men were randomised equally: 20/29 treated participants versus 7/26 placebo participants responded, P < 0.001. This per-protocol result establishes improvement under that protocol, not normal function.
milestones.set_by: Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, registered protocol NCT04050020; written for mild-to-moderate nonsurgical ED and excluding previous major pelvic surgery.
milestones.threshold_quote: patients in each group attaining MCID in the IIEF-EF domain from baseline to 6 months after the final treatment.

milestones.title: A finite treatment increases IIEF-EF recovery to ≥22 after a six-week drug-free washout.
milestones.criterion: A randomised placebo-controlled study demonstrates a higher proportion reaching IIEF-EF ≥22 after a six-week drug-free washout. REACTT tested nine months of tadalafil in 423 men after nerve-sparing prostatectomy: daily treatment n=139, on-demand treatment n=143 and placebo n=141. Recovery occurred in 20.9%, 16.9% and 19.1%, respectively; neither tadalafil comparison was significant, P=0.675 and P=0.704. This early postoperative study did not establish treatment of chronic post-prostatectomy ED.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly, REACTT protocol NCT01026818; this recovery definition was published for early rehabilitation after bilateral nerve-sparing prostatectomy.

milestones.title: A multicentre trial meets SMSNA's 2-, 5- or 7-point median erectile-function efficacy thresholds.
milestones.criterion: A prospective, adequately powered, multicentre randomised sham/placebo-controlled study demonstrates safety and a median between-group IIEF-EF benefit of ≥2 points for mild ED, ≥5 for moderate ED or ≥7 for severe ED; mixed populations use SMSNA's severity-weighted threshold. For a restorative claim, the trial must assess unassisted function after treatment and its durability under stated treatment restrictions. SMSNA specifies no common treatment-free interval. The cited human studies do not establish this combined result.
milestones.set_by: SMSNA, 2026 position statement defining clinical efficacy, combined with its 2021 requirement for multicentre restorative-therapy safety and efficacy studies; these efficacy thresholds do not define cure.
milestones.threshold_quote: 2-, 5-, or 7-point median improvements between groups among mild, moderate, or severe ED cohorts

not_found: No common regulator or society completion test specified a responder fraction, treatment-free interval and durability period for restoration after finite ED treatment.
The AUANews account of the 2026 SMSNA restorative-therapy update and the 70-man randomised adipose-cell study published in 2026 could not be opened successfully.
ClinicalTrials.gov records NCT01026818 and NCT02240823 rendered without study details; their endpoints were available in the peer-reviewed reports.

results.finding: In 63 rats with cavernous nerve injury, autologous SVF improved nerve-stimulated ICP/MAP versus saline controls (P < 0.05).
results.detail: SVF was injected immediately or four weeks after nerve injury. Erectile function was assessed 12 weeks after injury. The study used a rat model; it did not test men after prostatectomy.
results.quote: Recovery of erectile function was observed in both SVF treated groups. This was reflected by significantly increased ICP/MAP responses to cavernous nerve electrostimulation compared to the vehicle group.

results.finding: In 40 men treated with autologous bone marrow concentrate, no significant adverse effects were reported.
results.detail: The IRB-approved phase I trial primarily recruited men with vasculogenic ED. Safety and erectile-function scores were primary endpoints, with follow-up to six months. Participants were on optimized medical therapy.
results.quote: The procedures were well tolerated and no patients reported significant adverse effects

results.finding: In 21 men with post-prostatectomy erectile dysfunction, no serious adverse events occurred after autologous regenerative cell treatment.
results.detail: The phase I study used a single injection and followed patients for 12 months, with safety as the primary endpoint. The excerpt does not explicitly state that the protocol was approved.
results.quote: Results: No serious adverse events occurred, but 8 reversible minor events related to the liposuction were noted.

results.finding: In 60 men with mild or moderate ED, PRP increased six-month responders versus placebo by 42 percentage points.
results.detail: Per-protocol analysis: 20/29 PRP participants versus 7/26 placebo participants responded, P < 0.001. Other ED treatments were prohibited. This demonstrates improvement under the study protocol, not restoration of normal function.
results.quote:
At 6 months, a MCID was achieved by 20/29 (69%) patients in the PRP group compared to 7/26 (27%)
in the placebo group. The risk difference between the two groups was 42% (95%CI: 18 /C066), P < 0.001

results.finding: In 70 men with post-prostatectomy ED, ADRCs versus placebo showed no significant difference in erectile hardness scores (P = 0.85).
results.detail: Erectile hardness was a six-month secondary endpoint, but the source does not report the required IIEF-EF responder proportions or whether other ED treatments were prohibited.
results.quote: There was no significant difference between the two groups in IIEF-5 (p > 0.99) and EHS (p = 0.85) scores.

results.finding: In 81 men completing a multicentre ED trial, reported median IIEF-EF change was 5.1 with shock waves versus −2.2 with sham.
results.detail: The trial did not analyze results by ED etiology or severity, so a vasculogenic-specific result and the severity-weighted threshold cannot be established. The reported median changes also match differences between group means, creating ambiguity. PDE5 inhibitors were prohibited, but durability after treatment remains uncertain.
results.quote: The median change in the IIEF-EF score in the Li-ESWT and sham groups was 5.1 and −2.2 (p<0.001), respectively, at the 7-week follow-up;
